## Active

### D-059 — A library exposes its handler bindings under ILib.methods

> _2026-08-20 · core/blong · active_

`ILib.methods?: LibMethods` was added to `core/blong/types.ts`
(`LibMethods = {[m: string]: LibFn | undefined}`), so a `library()` factory returns its object
DIRECTLY and the conventional `methods` member holds the resolved handler bindings, typed through
ILib. Handlers destructure `lib: {methods = {}, ...}` (the default is needed because the member is
optional) and call `methods.<name>?.(...)`. Libraries do NOT re-export config constants — handlers
read `config` directly and the library keeps only the method resolution plus pure helpers;
`blong-login/sessionLib.ts` is the reference implementation with 11 `login.methods.*` bindings.
Trade-off: members other than `methods` are `LibFn` with unknown returns, so a call site needing a
precise type needs a generic (one place: `sha256Hex<string>` in a string comparison). Verified:
core/blong, blong-login, blong-access and blong-gogo lint green; tap access 37/37, party 15/15,
gateway 20/20, kopi 6/6; Playwright 21 passed.

### D-100 — IPlatformApi gained an optional mkdirSync for scaffolders

> _2026-09-12 · core/blong · active_

Scaffolders must create directories, and the alternative was requiring every caller to pre-create
them. It was added as optional so the browser stub stays valid.

### D-267 — A region in meta carries names, not the log position

> _2026-09-25 · core/blong · active_

The log keeps its own RegionMark with an id and pointsBefore, which describe a place in the
execution that minted them: a position is only meaningful inside the process that assigned it, so a
chain that arrived over the wire from another process would bring a number that means nothing
locally. The mark copied onto meta progress entries therefore keeps the three names only
(discriminator, candidates, chosen), and a report identifies a group by the chain of names rather
than by an id. pointsBefore is deliberately not copied either: it counts points still pending for
the next record, while the array counts everything announced, so the two would disagree.

### D-266 — One progress array on the invocation, replaced outright

> _2026-09-25 · core/blong · active_

meta.checkpoints and meta.decisions are gone, replaced by meta.progress, one array holding points
and branches in the order they were announced. Two arrays could not say where a branch sat relative
to the points: a report groups by the region chain each entry names, and the order is what makes the
nesting visible. Each entry is record-shaped (kind point with name, data and timestamp; kind region
with discriminator, candidates, chosen, values) and both shapes name the branches they sat inside.
No alias was left behind, and the transport field was renamed with it: the JSON-RPC response, the
MLE envelope and the receive codec carry progress, so a caller collects what a callee announced
under the name the callee used. The demo scenarios reach the handlers over that wire and assert on
their own meta.progress, which is what exercised the rename; their run does not complete yet (see
the demo friction and todo entries).

### D-280 — Progress reports double their gap, up to five minutes

> _2026-09-26 · core/blong · active_

The progress reporting of a long step now backs off instead of repeating on a fixed cadence: the
first report comes when the step crosses `thresholdMs`, and each later one comes after twice the gap
of the one before it, capped at `MAX_PROGRESS_INTERVAL_MS` (five minutes). A step that ran an hour
used to print a line every five seconds, which is the excessive logging the reporting exists to
avoid; with defaults it now prints at 1 s, 6 s, 16 s, 36 s, 76 s, 156 s and then every five minutes.

Two things to know before changing the options. `withProgress` is declared in three places — the
implementation in `core/blong-lib/index.ts`, the `withProgress` entry on the lib surface in
`core/blong/types.ts`, and `ILogger.progress` on the same file — so an option added to one is
silently unusable from the other two, which is what happened to `slowMs` until it was noticed while
adding this one: the runtime forwards its options wholesale, so only the types were wrong. And the
cap applies to the gap, not to the count: a step that never finishes keeps reporting, just rarely.
